name: Adam und Eva
access: Free, public forest (Badenburger Wald); no access restriction found.
transport: Not verified; no confirmed nearby stop. Wieseck is a district on Gießen's northeast edge, reachable by car or bicycle from the city centre.
verify_notes: Twin sessile oaks (a pair, both counted as one designated monument), officially a Naturdenkmal and Baumveteran-registered pair, documented in Hans Joachim Froehlich's 1990 book on historic trees. Girth figures disagree slightly between sources: the official Giessen Naturdenkmal register (via de.wikipedia) gives approx. 420cm and 520cm for the two trees, heights approx. 25m and 30m; monumentale-eichen.de and baumkunde.de (2020 measurement) give 442cm and 595cm, height 33m for the larger of the two. Recorded the larger/more recent figures; both sets are real disagreement, not error, and should be flagged for the reader. One tree has a striking, monumental unbranched trunk over 10m tall before the first branch. Part of the Giessen cluster: 5.4km from the Rödgen pair (gie_002/gie_003) and roughly 9km from the Lützellinden group (gie_004), so a Giessen page reads as three separate district stops rather than one walk.

name: Alte Eiche

location.address: Corner of Geiselweg/Seeweg, Rödgen, Gießen, on a former forest picnic clearing

access: Free, public clearing off Seeweg; no restriction found.
transport: Not verified; no confirmed nearby stop. Rödgen is a district on Gießen's south edge, reachable by car or bicycle from the city centre.
verify_notes: Under state protection since 3 September 1906, one of the oldest protection dates found in this batch. Official Giessen Naturdenkmal register gives ca. 275-300 years, 16m tall, 610cm girth; monumentale-eichen.de gives ca. 350 years, 15m, 629cm girth (measured 2018); recorded the more recent measured figure and flagged the disagreement. Trunk shows real decline: a triangular opening sealed with a grating on one side, bark missing on the other, a horizontal branch propped on two steel tubes; still described as vital overall. Roughly 410m from the Schillerlinde (gie_003), walkable together as one stop of the Giessen page.

name: Schillerlinde

location.address: Geiselstrauchkopf, edge of Rödgen, Gießen, near the sports field

access: Free, on municipal ground near the sports field; no restriction found.
transport: Not verified; no confirmed nearby stop. Rödgen is a district on Gießen's south edge, reachable by car or bicycle from the city centre.
verify_notes: Planted 11 November 1859 for the 100th birthday of Friedrich von Schiller, one of hundreds planted across German towns that Schiller year; officially a Naturdenkmal. Rare case in this batch with a genuinely documented planting date, so the age is exact rather than estimated (167 years as of 2026). Modest size for its age (197cm girth): a memorial tree rather than a giant, which the story should say plainly rather than oversell. A local page (spd-roedgen.de) reportedly ties it to a historical village protest tradition (Grenzgang) but that page 403'd on this and an earlier pass and was not independently confirmed; leave that detail out or mark it unconfirmed. Only ~410m from the Alte Eiche (gie_002), walkable together as one stop.

name: Lindengruppe an der Lindbachquelle

location.address: At the Lindbach spring source, Lützellinden, Gießen

access: Free, public spring/parkland site in Lützellinden; no restriction found.
transport: Not verified; no confirmed nearby stop. Lützellinden is a district on Gießen's southwest edge, reachable by car or bicycle from the city centre.
verify_notes: Officially designated Naturdenkmal, 'landschaftsbildprägend' (landscape-defining), a small group of winter lindens standing together at the source of the Lindbach: originally three, now two survive after one fell in a storm, plus a young replacement planted by NABU after the spring area was renaturalised. Both sources agree the pair is 200-400 years old (register gives that as a range for the group; baumkunde's individual measurement is of the older, larger tree: 579cm girth, 15m tall, measured 30 May 2020). The oldest of the pair has been damaged by fire twice and by repeated storm and lightning strikes; baumkunde's most recent visit (10 Feb 2021) still describes it as vital though partially hollow. Coordinates from the two sources agree almost exactly (baumkunde E8 36.031/N50 32.537 = 8.60052,50.54228; Wikipedia's Naturdenkmal register 50.542265,8.600680), so this is tree-level confirmed. Completes the Giessen cluster to four verified trees across three district stops (Wieseck, Rödgen x2, Lützellinden), clearing the 4-tree floor for a Giessen page. NOTE FOR WRITER: the three stops are several km apart within Gießen (not one walk); label honestly as a city page with multiple stops rather than a single afternoon walk.
